question.instructions: Which visual defect does this rendered slide show? Judge only what the image shows, using the deck facts beside it. A slide is poorly designed when its visual arrangement makes its message harder to find or read than the content requires; choose the option that names how. Do not invent defects: wording, facts, taste, colour preference, consistently applied style choices and the composition the designer chose are not defects, a slide does not need more images, icons or text than it has, and an option applies only when the image plainly shows it. Choose none for a slide a careful designer would deliver as it is.

options.none: The slide is clean: none of the other options applies.
options.overlap: The drawn areas of elements cover each other: text over text, text over a picture or a shape, a logo over a title, parts drawn on top of parts.
options.weak_hierarchy: The eye cannot tell what matters first: the title is not the most prominent text on the slide, being smaller, lighter or fainter than the body, or emphasis is spread so evenly that nothing leads the eye.
options.cramped: Content is squeezed or too small for its space: long paragraphs filling their boxes, lines pressed together, parts touching, text too small to read comfortably.
options.wasted_space: A large empty area serves no purpose: the parts fill a small part of the slide, or a block of the slide is blank while other content is squeezed.
options.misaligned: Edges or baselines that should line up do not: parts of one row or grid sit at different heights or offsets, or columns start at different positions.
options.unbalanced: Visual weight sits to one side with no reason: heavy content on one side and a large empty or faint area on the other.
options.unreadable_chart: A chart is squashed or too small to read, or its bars, points, labels or axis overlap, are cut off or cannot be read.
options.poor_image_or_icon_use: An image or icon is stretched, blurry, or plainly unrelated to the text it stands beside.
options.off_design_system: A background, text color or title style breaks from the deck's design system in the facts: a color outside its palette, or a title whose size, weight or alignment differs from the deck's other titles.
options.hero_metric_template: A big number with a small caption under it, set in an accent color, is the whole design of the slide, the generic stat-hero template, where the number does not carry the point of the slide.
options.rough_illustration: A drawn illustration or diagram that looks crude: uneven shapes, clumsy proportions, hand-made vector art that a designer would not ship.
options.monotonous_spacing: Every gap, padding and margin on the slide is the same, so nothing groups or separates: parts that belong together sit as far apart as parts that do not.
options.fake_sequence_numbering: Items carry numbers or step labels although their content has no order, so the numbering invents a sequence.
options.other_visual: Another visual defect you can point to in the image. Not wording, facts, layout choice or taste.

deck.instructions: Does this slide's arrangement show a pattern across the deck? The image shows every slide of the deck at reduced size, each under its number. Do not invent defects: a title slide or a closing slide that differs from the rest, one palette and one typeface on every slide, and a header or footer that recurs are not defects. Choose none for a slide a careful designer would deliver as it is.

options.none: The slide shows no such pattern.
options.repetitive_layout: This slide arranges its parts the way at least one other content slide does, the same grid of cards, the same split, the same list, so the deck reads as one slide repeated.
options.inconsistent_style: This slide's colours, typefaces, shapes or title treatment differ from the rest of the deck without a reason.

fixer.instructions:
You repair the visual design of one slide in a deck. You get an image of how the slide renders, what a visual reviewer saw in it (defect kinds with the reviewer's probability for each), the defects the build measured, and edits: the repairs that can be applied to this slide, each with an id and a description, each already checked against the build's rules. Answer with the id of the one edit that best removes those defects and one sentence saying what it changes.

Rules:
- Choose from edits only. Do not write markup, and do not invent an id.
- Choose the edit whose arrangement suits the content in the image and removes the defects named: an empty area or a part pushed to one side calls for an arrangement that fills the slide, a squeezed one for an arrangement with more room.
- repetitive_layout and inconsistent_style come from a contact sheet of the whole deck, the second image: for repetitive_layout choose an arrangement that differs from the slides that look like this one, for inconsistent_style choose the arrangement closest to the deck's other slides.
- When refusedLastTime is present the build refused the edit chosen before for that reason: choose a different edit.
- Edits keep the words, numbers, tables, charts, pictures and speaker notes as they are.
